The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

</profile>

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy
The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027 and abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely. The "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure state pensions and pensioner tax allowances rise with inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit thresholds would shift to household income, starting withdrawal at £120,000 combined income.

## Taxation and Spending
The party commits to no increases in income tax, VAT, or Capital Gains Tax. Public sector net debt must fall, with borrowing below 3% of GDP. Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030. The civil service would return to pre-pandemic size, with reduced spending on consultants and diversity initiatives.

## Immigration
A legal cap on migration would be introduced, with annual parliamentary votes. The Rwanda removal scheme would operate monthly flights. Visa fees would increase, and health checks would be required for migrants. Asylum claims would be processed within six months.

## Housing
The target is 1.6 million homes in England, focusing on brownfield development. First-time buyers would pay no Stamp Duty on homes up to £425,000. A new Help to Buy scheme would offer 20% equity loans. Leasehold reforms would cap ground rents at £250.

## Healthcare
NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, recruiting 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors. Pharmacy First would expand, with 250 GP surgeries built or modernised. Social care costs would be capped from October 2025.

## Education and Youth
Mandatory National Service would offer military or civic service options for 18-year-olds. The Advanced British Standard would replace A-Levels and T-Levels. Mobile phones would be banned during school hours. 100,000 additional apprenticeships would be funded by closing underperforming university courses.

## Energy and Environment
Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds would continue. Offshore wind capacity would treble. Two Small Modular Reactor fleets would be approved. No new green levies would be introduced, and the £2 bus fare cap would continue throughout the parliament.

## Transport
£36 billion from HS2 savings would fund local transport, including £8.3 billion for road repairs. Great British Railways would be established. Road pricing would be banned, and London's ULEZ expansion reversed.

## Welfare Reform
Disability benefit assessments would be reformed, with mental health support potentially replacing cash payments. Benefit claims would close after 12 months if suitable jobs are refused. Fraud measures would receive enhanced powers.

## Devolution
The UK internal market would be protected. Funding would continue directly to Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland communities. The Windsor Framework commitments would be implemented for Northern Ireland.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Mental health services would receive investment to achieve parity with physical health, including counsellors in all schools. A National Cancer Control Plan and measures to end new HIV cases by 2030 are included.

## Social Care
The manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment for free personal care, increased carer pay with a career structure, and £3bn additional funding for children's social care. Disability benefits would increase by 5%.

## Housing
Plans include building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy
The manifesto targets wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, ending new oil and gas licences and fossil fuel subsidies, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Community ownership of energy infrastructure would be encouraged. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy
Proposed spending includes £40bn average annual investment in green economic transformation. Railways, water companies, and major retail energy companies would return to public ownership. A wealth tax of 1-2% on assets above £10m would be introduced, alongside capital gains tax reform and alignment of investment income taxation with employment income rates.

## Employment
The manifesto proposes a £15/hour minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repeal of anti-union legislation, and a four-day working week. Gig economy workers would receive full employment rights.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, the five-week benefit wait would end, and the bedroom tax would be scrapped. Carer's allowance would increase by at least 10%.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would give legal personhood to nature. 30% of land and seas would be protected by 2030. Water companies would be nationalised. A new Right to Roam Act for England is proposed.

## Education
School funding would increase by £8bn, including £2.5bn annually for building repairs. Tuition fees would be scrapped and maintenance grants restored. SEND provision would receive £5bn investment.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with railways returning to public ownership. £2.5bn annually would fund cycleways and footpaths. Free bus travel for under-18s is proposed. New petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment, creating safe asylum routes, abolishing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, and permitting asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## Foreign Policy
The party supports an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident. Overseas aid would increase to 1% of GNI by 2033.

## Funding
Revenue measures include wealth taxes, carbon taxes, and business tax reforms estimated to raise £170bn+ by 2030. Additional borrowing would fund capital investment.
